# 1. Data Import

```{r}









control = 'mtx_data/control'
malignant_dir = 'mtx_data/malignant'

healthy <- Read10X(control)
malignant <- Read10X(malignant_dir)
```

## 2. Merging samples

```{r}
# Healthy
H <- as.matrix(healthy)
colnames(H) <- paste(colnames(H),"H", sep = "_")

# Malignant
M <- as.matrix(malignant)
colnames(M) <- paste(colnames(M),"M", sep = "_")

x <- cbind(H, M)

# we remove these file to save memory.
rm(H, M)
rm(healthy, malignant)
```

# 3. Seurat Object Instantiation

```{r Seurat-Object}
# Seurat Object Instantiation
seu <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = x, project = "RNA-pro")

# Condition Annotation
seu$condition <- ifelse(
  str_split(string = colnames(seu), pattern = "_", simplify = TRUE)[,2] == "H",
  "Healthy",
  "Malignant"
)

# Mitochondrial Genes Percentage Quantification
seu[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(seu, pattern = "^MT-")

# Seurat Object Metadata Exploration
# view(seu@meta.data)
```

## Saving

```{r}
saveRDS(seu, "checkpoints/seu.rds")
```

### 4.1.5 Cell Filtration

```{r Cell-Filtration}
# Classical QC
ncol(seu) #13685

seu_subset <- subset(seu, subset = (nCount_RNA > counts_thresholds[1]) & (nCount_RNA < counts_thresholds[2]) & (nFeature_RNA > features_thresholds[1]) & (nFeature_RNA < features_thresholds[2]) & (percent.mt < 15))

ncol(seu_subset) #12761

# Saving memory
rm(seu)
```

## 4.2 Genes QC

-   This filtration step will remove all features that do not have non-zero accounts in at least 3 cells.

```{r Gene-QC}
nrow(seu_subset) #33538

filter3 <- function(seurat){
  #Threshold
  threshold <- 3
  #Raw Counts
  counts <- seurat@assays$RNA$`counts`
  rawcounts <- as.matrix(counts)
  #Number of cells where expression is greater than zero for each gene
  sums <- rowSums(rawcounts > 0)
  #Genes that are expressed in a number of cells greater than threshold
  sums_2 <- sums[sums > threshold]
  #Filtering and dimensions of Seurat object before and after
  seurat <- seurat[names(sums_2),]
  return(seurat)
}

seu_subset <- filter3(seurat = seu_subset)

nrow(seu_subset) #18546
```

```{r PCA, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}

seu_subset <- RunPCA(seu_subset)

# Visualization
#Phase
do_DimPlot(
  seu_subset,
  group.by = "Phase",
  pt.size = 1.5,
  plot.title = "Phase",
  plot.axes = T)

ggsave(filename = "write/figures/Cell Cycle Phase PCA.png",

do_DimPlot(
  seu_subset,
  group.by = "condition",
  pt.size = 1.5,
  plot.title = "Condition",
  plot.axes = T)

ggsave(filename = "write/figures/Condition PCA.png",
```


### 8.1.3 Cell Cycle Regression

-   Given that the focus of this analysis is not cell cycle-driven variation, we will regress out cell cycle variation using `SCTransform()`, as is shown in the code below. We then run PCA on the updated count matrices and re-do the visualizations to ensure that cell cycle variation is no longer a primary driver.

```{r PCA-CellCycleRegression, fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
# SCTransform (Cell Cycle Regression)
seu_subset <- suppressWarnings(SCTransform(object = seu_subset, 
                                           variable.features.n = 3000, 
                                           vars.to.regress = "Phase"))
# PCA
seu_subset <- RunPCA(seu_subset, 
              features = VariableFeatures(object = seu_subset), 
              verbose = FALSE)
```

After regression of the cell cycle above, we will re-do the visualizations:

```{r PCA-CellCycleRegression-plots}
# Visualisation
do_DimPlot(seu_subset, 
           reduction = "pca", 
           dims = c(1,2), 
           group.by = "Phase", 
           pt.size = 1.5,
           plot.axes = T)

ggsave(filename = "write/figures/Cell Cycle Phase PCA (After Cell Cycle Regression).png",
       height = 10,
       width = 15)

do_DimPlot(seu_subset, 
        reduction = "pca", 
        dims = c(4,5), 
        group.by = "condition", 
        pt.size = 1.5, 
        plot.axes = T,
        split.by = "condition")

ggsave(filename = "write/figures/Condition PCA (After Cell Cycle Regression).png",
       height = 10,
       width = 15)
```

# 9. Differential Expression Analysis

## 9. FindMarkers

```{r}
markers <- FindMarkers(
  seu_subset,
  group.by = "condition",
  ident.1 = "Malignant",
  ident.2 = "Healthy",
  test.use = "wilcox",
  logfc.threshold = 0.25,
  min.pct = 0.10)

# Saving the markers as a table
# Adding gene names and regulation annotation to the table
markers_export <- markers %>% 
  rownames_to_column(var = "gene") %>%            
  mutate(regulation = ifelse(avg_log2FC > 0,
                             "Up", 
                             "Down"))
write_csv(
  markers_export,
  "write/tables/Markers.csv"
)
```

## 9.2 Visualization

### 9.2.1 Volcano Plot

```{r}
EnhancedVolcano(
  markers,
  lab = rownames(markers),
  x = "avg_log2FC",
  y = "p_val_adj",
  title = "Healthy vs Malignant cells",
  pCutoff = 0.05,
  FCcutoff = 0.25,
  labSize = 3,
  xlim = c(-10,10))

ggsave(filename = "write/figures/Volcano Plot.png",
       height = 10,
       width = 15)
```

### 9.2.2 Condition Heatmap

```{r}
DoHeatmap(
```

# Splitting the Seurat Object into Two Objects by Condition

```{r}
malignant_obj <- subset(seu_subset, subset = condition == "Malignant")

healthy_obj   <- subset(seu_subset, subset = condition == "Healthy")
```

# 10. Clustering

## 10.1 Louvain Clustering (Multiple Resolutions)

```{r Clustering}
# Healthy
for(i in seq(0,1,0.1)){
healthy_obj <- healthy_obj %>%
  FindNeighbors(reduction = "pca",
                dims = 1:20,
                verbose = F) %>%
  FindClusters(resolution = i,
               verbose = F)
}

# Malignant
for(i in seq(0,1,0.1)){
malignant_obj <- malignant_obj %>%
  FindNeighbors(reduction = "pca",
                dims = 1:20,
                verbose = F) %>%
  FindClusters(resolution = i,
               verbose = F)
}
```

# 12. Cell Type annotation

## **12.1 Healthy**

### 12.1.1 **Cluster-based**

```{r}
all_markers <- FindAllMarkers(
  healthy_obj,
  group.by = "seurat_clusters",
  only.pos = TRUE,
  logfc.threshold = 0.050,
  min.pct = 0.15,
  return.thresh = 0.05
)


ref <- celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData()

expression_matrix <- GetAssayData(healthy_obj, layer = 'data', assay = "RNA")
  
clusters <- healthy_obj$seurat_clusters
exp.matrix <- as.SingleCellExperiment(healthy_obj,slot = 'data', assay = "RNA")


singler_clusters <- SingleR(
  test = expression_matrix,
  ref = ref,
  labels = ref$label.main,
  clusters = clusters
)


cell_classes <- singler_clusters$pruned.labels

names(cell_classes) <- levels(healthy_obj$seurat_clusters)

healthy_obj$annotated_clusters <- unname(cell_classes[as.character(healthy_obj$seurat_clusters)])

unique(healthy_obj$annotated_clusters)
```

### **12.1.2 Cell-based**

```{r}

all_markers <- FindAllMarkers(
  healthy_obj,
  group.by = "seurat_clusters",
  only.pos = TRUE,
  logfc.threshold = 0.050,
  min.pct = 0.15,
  return.thresh = 0.05
)


ref <- celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData()

expression_matrix <- GetAssayData(healthy_obj, layer = 'data', assay = "RNA")
  
clusters <- healthy_obj$seurat_clusters
exp.matrix <- as.SingleCellExperiment(healthy_obj,slot = 'data', assay = "RNA")


singler_clusters <- SingleR(
  test = expression_matrix,
  ref = ref,
  labels = ref$label.main,
)


cell_classes <- singler_clusters$pruned.labels


healthy_obj$annotated_cells <- cell_classes
healthy_obj <- subset(healthy_obj, subset = !is.na(annotated_cells))

unique(healthy_obj$annotated_cells)

# Plotting cell type UMAP
do_DimPlot(
  healthy_obj,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "annotated_cells",
  plot.axes = T,
  label = T,
  repel = T,
  pt.size = 1.5
)
ggsave(
  filename = "write/figures/SingleR cell type annotation UMAP (Healthy).png",
  height = 10,
  width = 15
)
```

```{r}
  only.pos = TRUE,
  logfc.threshold = 0.050,
  min.pct = 0.15,
  return.thresh = 0.05
)



ref <- celldex::HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData()

expression_matrix <- GetAssayData(malignant_obj, layer = 'data', assay = "RNA")
  
clusters <- malignant_obj$seurat_clusters



singler_clusters <- SingleR(
  test = expression_matrix,
  ref = ref,
  labels = ref$label.main,
)


cell_classes <- singler_clusters$pruned.labels
malignant_obj$annotated_cells <- cell_classes
malignant_obj <- subset(malignant_obj, subset = !is.na(annotated_cells))

unique(malignant_obj$annotated_cells)

# Plotting cell type UMAP
do_DimPlot(
  malignant_obj,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "annotated_cells",
  plot.axes = T,
  label = T,
  repel = T,
  pt.size = 1.5
) 
ggsave(
  filename = "write/figures/SingleR cell type annotation UMAP (Malignant).png",
  height = 10,
  width = 15
)
```

## 12.3 Excluding non-shared Cell Types

```{r}
# Cell types present in both malignant and healthy
shared_types <- intersect(
  unique(malignant_obj$annotated_cells),
  unique(healthy_obj$annotated_cells)
)

# Filtering malignant
malignant_obj <- subset(
  malignant_obj,
  subset = annotated_cells %in% shared_types
)

# Filtering healthy
healthy_obj <- subset(
  healthy_obj,
  subset = annotated_cells %in% shared_types
)

# Inspecting
unique(healthy_obj$annotated_cells)
unique(malignant_obj$annotated_cells)
```

# 13. CellChat

## 13.1 Creating CellChat Objects from the Seurat Objects

```{r}
# Healthy:
chat_healthy <- createCellChat(healthy_obj, group.by = "annotated_cells")

# Attaching the human LR database to the object and keeping only secreted signalling genes
chat_healthy@DB <- CellChatDB.human

# subsetting the expression data of signaling genes
chat_healthy <- subsetData(chat_healthy)

# Inspecting available group names
levels(chat_healthy@idents)

# Malignant:
chat_malignant <- createCellChat(malignant_obj, group.by = "annotated_cells")

# Attaching the human LR database to the object and keeping only secreted signalling genes
chat_malignant@DB <- CellChatDB.human

# subsetting the expression data of signaling genes
chat_malignant <- subsetData(chat_malignant)

# Inspecting available group names
levels(chat_malignant@idents)
```

**Healthy sample cell types:**

```         
[1] "B_cell"           "BM"               "CMP"              "Erythroblast"     "GMP"              "HSC_-G-CSF"
[7] "MEP"              "Monocyte"         "Myelocyte"        "Neutrophils"      "NK_cell"          "Platelets"
[13] "Pre-B_cell_CD34-" "Pro-B_cell_CD34+" "Pro-Myelocyte"    "T_cells"         
```

**Malignant sample cell types:**

```         
[1] "B_cell"           "BM"               "CMP"              "Erythroblast"     "GMP"              "HSC_-G-CSF"
[7] "MEP"              "Monocyte"         "Myelocyte"        "Neutrophils"      "NK_cell"          "Platelets"
[13] "Pre-B_cell_CD34-" "Pro-B_cell_CD34+" "Pro-Myelocyte"    "T_cells"         
```

## 13.2 Pre-processing & Communication Inference for Both Samples

```{r}
# Healthy:

# Identifying over-expressed genes and interactions
chat_healthy <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(chat_healthy)
chat_healthy <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(chat_healthy)
# The number of highly variable ligand-receptor pairs used for signaling inference is 454

# Computing communication probability & filtering low-cell groups
chat_healthy <- computeCommunProb(chat_healthy, type = "triMean")
chat_healthy <- filterCommunication(chat_healthy, min.cells = 10)
#The cell-cell communication related with the following cell groups are excluded due to the few number of cells:  MEP, Pro-B_cell_CD34+ ! 	20.8% interactions are removed!

# Inferring pathway-level communication
chat_healthy <- computeCommunProbPathway(chat_healthy)
chat_healthy <- aggregateNet(chat_healthy)

# Inspecting the signalling pathways inferred
unique(chat_healthy@netP$pathways)

# Malignant:

# Identifying over-expressed genes and interactions
chat_malignant <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(chat_malignant)
chat_malignant <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(chat_malignant)
# The number of highly variable ligand-receptor pairs used for signaling inference is 502 

# Computing communication probability & filtering low-cell groups
chat_malignant <- computeCommunProb(chat_malignant, type = "triMean")
chat_malignant <- filterCommunication(chat_malignant, min.cells = 10)
#The cell-cell communication related with the following cell groups are excluded due to the few number of cells:  BM, Platelets, Pro-B_cell_CD34+ ! 	27.8% interactions are removed!


# Inferring pathway-level communication
chat_malignant <- computeCommunProbPathway(chat_malignant)
chat_malignant <- aggregateNet(chat_malignant)

# Inspecting the signalling pathways inferred
unique(chat_malignant@netP$pathways)
```

## 13.4 Visualization

### 13.4.1 Total Interaction Counts & Weights

```{r}
gg1 <- compareInteractions(cellchat, show.legend = FALSE, group = c(1,2))

gg2 <- compareInteractions(cellchat, show.legend = FALSE, group = c(1,2), measure = "weight")

gg1 + gg2

ggsave(
  "write/figures/total_interaction_counts_weights.png",
  plot = gg1 + gg2,
  width = 12,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300)
```

### 13.4.2 Differential Interaction Networks

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(1,2), xpd = TRUE)

# Counts
netVisual_diffInteraction(cellchat, weight.scale = TRUE)

# Weights
netVisual_diffInteraction(cellchat, weight.scale = TRUE, measure = "weight")
```

### 13.4.3 Heatmaps of Interaction Counts and Weights

```{r}
ht1 <- netVisual_heatmap(cellchat)

ht2 <- netVisual_heatmap(cellchat, measure = "weight")

combined_ht <- ht1 + ht2

combined_ht

png("write/figures/heatmaps_interaction_count_weight.png",
    width  = 3000, height = 2000, res = 300)

ComplexHeatmap::draw(combined_ht, heatmap_legend_side = "right")

dev.off()
```

### 13.4.4 Circle Plots - Total Interaction Count  &  Strength (Healthy vs Malignant)

```{r}
#Count
weight.max <- getMaxWeight(object.list, attribute = c("idents","count"))

par(mfrow = c(1,2), xpd=TRUE)
for (i in 1:length(object.list)) {
  netVisual_circle(object.list[[i]]@net$count,
                   weight.scale = T,
                   label.edge= F,
                   edge.weight.max = weight.max[2],
                   edge.width.max = 12,
                   title.name = paste0("Number of interactions - ",
                                       names(object.list)[i]))
}

# Weight
weight.max <- getMaxWeight(object.list, attribute = c("idents", "weight"))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), xpd = TRUE)
for (i in seq_along(object.list)) {
  netVisual_circle(object.list[[i]]@net$weight,
                   weight.scale    = TRUE,
                   label.edge      = FALSE,
                   edge.weight.max = weight.max[2],
                   edge.width.max  = 12,
                   title.name      = paste0("Interaction strength – ",
                                             names(object.list)[i]))
}
```

### 13.4.5 Signaling Role Scatter Plot

```{r}
num.link <- sapply(
  object.list,
  function(x) {rowSums(x@net$count) +
      colSums(x@net$count) - diag(x@net$count)})

weight.MinMax <- c(min(num.link), max(num.link))

gg <- list()

for (i in 1:length(object.list)) {
  gg[[i]] <- netAnalysis_signalingRole_scatter(object.list[[i]], title = names(object.list)[i], weight.MinMax = weight.MinMax)
}

#Combines all scatter plots into a single panel 
scatter_combined <- patchwork::wrap_plots(plots = gg)

scatter_combined
ggsave(
  "write/figures/signaling_role_scatter.png",
  scatter_combined,
  width = 15,
  height = 10,
  dpi = 300)
```

### 13.4.6 Bubble Plots (T-Cells & B-Cells)

```{r}
# Showing all the significant interactions (L-R pairs) associated with the following specific pathway

pathways.show <- c("MIF", "GALECTIN", "ANNEXIN")

for (pw in pathways.show) {
  p <- netVisual_bubble(
         cellchat,
         signaling = pw,          # one pathway at a time
         angle.x   = 45,
         comparison = c(1,2)
       ) +
    plot_annotation(
         title = paste("Bubble plot of signals of ", pw, "Pathway Genes")
       )

  print(p)

  ggsave(sprintf("write/figures/bubble_%s.png", pw), p,
         width = 10, height = 15, dpi = 300)
}
```

### 13.4.7 Hierarchy Plots (MIF, GALECTIN, ANNEXIN)

```{r}

for (pw in pathways.show) {
  max.w <- getMaxWeight(object.list, slot.name = "netP", attribute = pw)[1]
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2), xpd = TRUE)
  for (i in seq_along(object.list)) {
    netVisual_aggregate(object.list[[i]], signaling = pw, layout = "circle",
                        edge.weight.max = max.w, edge.width.max = 10,
                        signaling.name = paste(pw, names(object.list)[i]))
  }
}
```

### 13.4.8 Gene Expression Violin Plot (MIF, GALECTIN, ANNEXIN)

```{r}
cellchat@meta$datasets <- factor(
  cellchat@meta$datasets,
  levels = c("Healthy", "Malignant"))

for (pw in pathways.show) {
  p <- plotGeneExpression(
    cellchat,
    signaling = pw,
    split.by = "datasets",
    colors.ggplot = TRUE,
    type = "violin") +
    plot_annotation(
         title = paste("Expression of", pw, "Pathway Genes"),
         subtitle = "Healthy = red  |  Malignant = teal"
       )  
  
  print(p)

  ggsave(sprintf("write/figures/gene_expression_%s_violin.png", pw), p,
         width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
}
```
